title: Creatine vs Protein: Which One Actually Builds Muscle?

scenes.title: HOOK
scenes.narration: Creatine or protein. If you could only pick *one*, which actually builds more muscle? The answer is not what the supplement aisle wants you to hear.

scenes.title: INTRODUCTION
scenes.narration: Here's the thing. They're not rivals. They do completely different jobs. *Protein* is the building material. *Creatine* is extra fuel for your hardest reps.

scenes.title: MAIN EDUCATION - PROTEIN
scenes.narration: Hard training stresses your muscle fibres, and protein supplies the bricks to rebuild them bigger. Research suggests about *one point six grams* per kilogram of body weight a day captures most of the benefit. Chicken, eggs, Greek yogurt, beans. A shake is just convenient food, not magic.

scenes.title: MAIN EDUCATION - CREATINE
scenes.narration: Creatine tops up the quick energy your muscles use in short, heavy efforts. That can mean an extra rep or two per set, and over months, those reps add up. It's one of the most studied supplements out there. Three to five grams a day, every day, any time.

scenes.title: VISUAL DEMONSTRATION
scenes.narration: Same set, same weight. With full creatine stores, you might squeeze out one more clean rep. Heads up, the scale can jump a kilogram or two at first. That's water in the muscle, not fat.

scenes.title: KEY TAKEAWAYS
scenes.narration: So which wins? *Protein*, because creatine can't build what you never eat. Nail your protein first. Then add creatine if you want a small, proven edge. If you have kidney problems, check with your doctor before taking either.

scenes.title: ENDING
scenes.narration: Bricks first, fuel second. Follow for more training science without the hype.
